S3.Thmtheorem1.text: Lemma 3.1. If $n$ is a primitive covering number then $P^{+}(n)\leq\tau\left(\frac{n}{P^{+}(n)}\right).$ (4)

S4.Thmtheorem10.text: Lemma 4.10. Suppose that $M=\{m_{1},m_{2},\ldots m_{k}\}$ is any set (or multiset) of moduli. Then the proportion of integers covered by any residue system whose moduli are the elements of $M$ is at most $\sum_{m\in M}\frac{1}{m}\ -\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}m,m^{\prime}\in M\\ \gcd(m,m^{\prime})=1\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{mm^{\prime}}\ +\ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}m,m^{\prime}\!,m^{\prime\prime}\in M\\ \text{ pairwise coprime}\end{subarray}}\frac{1}{mm^{\prime}m^{\prime\prime}}\ -\ \cdots\ =\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}S\subseteq M,\ S\neq\emptyset\\ S\text{ pairwise coprime}\end{subarray}}\frac{(-1)^{|S|+1}}{\lcm S}.$

S4.Thmtheorem11.text: Theorem 4.11. If an integer $n$ factors as $n=\ell b$ where $\ell$ and $b$ are coprime and $\ell$ is an almost-covering number, then $c(n)\leq 1+\frac{\ell-1}{\ell}+\frac{1}{\ell}\sum_{d\mid b,d>1}\frac{B(\tau(\ell),\omega(d))}{d}.$ (11)

section_4_definitions.r: For a positive integer n we first define r(n) to be the maximum cardinality of the set of residues that can be covered by a set of congruences with distinct moduli greater than 1, each dividing n.

definition_4_5.text: We call an integer n an almost-covering number if r(n)=n-1.

theorem_4_11_proof_multiplicity.text: Since each divisor of b appears with multiplicity tau(ell) in M, any fixed subset S of D(b) appears tau(ell)^|S| times in the sum.

definition_5_1.text: If P^-(b)=p_(j+1)<=tau(ell) then n is a covering number by Corollary 4.8 and we define cprime(n)=2, otherwise we define the displayed Bell-polynomial expression.
definition_5_1.scope: This later trivial-bound branch applies to n=1920 and is not refuted by its Theorem 4.11 counterexample.

definition_4_7.text: For even n, take j to be the largest initial prime index such that (9) holds for every preceding step; ell(n) is the product of those first j full prime powers. For odd n, ell(n)=1.
definition_4_7.example: For 1920=2^7*3*5, the next prime3 differs from tau(128)+1=9, so j=1 and ell(1920)=128.
